CBJ.head: We had Columbus as slight underdogs (43%), and it went Utah’s way.

UTA.head: We leaned Utah’s way (57%), and they came through.

surprises.head: Utah’s power play feasted on Columbus’s kill
surprises.body: Columbus has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 3 power-play goals on 4 chances. A power play like theirs against a kill like Columbus’s scores 3 or more about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: Columbus got the good looks
surprises.body: Utah usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Columbus’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Schmaltz reaches 500 points as the Mammoth beat the Blue Jackets
paras: Cossa was back in an NHL net for the first time since Dec 9, 2024, and got the win. Mikhail Sergachev opened the scoring for the Mammoth on the power play midway through the first. Nick Schmaltz made it 2-0 less than five minutes later, with Clayton Keller picking up his 600th NHL point on the assist. Kent Johnson got the Blue Jackets on the board early in the second, but that was as close as they got. Dylan Guenther stretched the lead to 3-1 on the power play early in the third. Schmaltz scored again on the power play with less than six minutes left to make it 4-1, his 500th NHL point. Guenther finished with a goal and two assists.

The Mammoth outshot the Blue Jackets 31-19, but the Blue Jackets’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Sebastian Cossa made his first NHL start and got the win. Jet Greaves stopped 27 of 31 for the Jackets.

The Mammoth went 3-for-4 on the power play. The Mammoth moved to 2-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage. The Blue Jackets fell to 1-1-0, giving up the best points percentage in the NHL to the Mammoth.

items.text: The Blue Jackets were without Damon Severson, Ivan Provorov, Dante Fabbro and others. Counting how much each missing player usually brings, no team was missing more at the time.
Neither of the preview’s calls held.
